Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: tool
candidates.comment: A tool relation between instructions or a direction and an object used but not consumed during the performance. Also called instrument, implement, equipment. Examples: "HowTo tool 'hammer'", "HowToDirection tool 'screwdriver'", "Recipe tool 'mixing bowl'". Distinct from instrument, which is a more general property for any object used in an action.

candidates.label: usedToDiagnose
candidates.comment: A used to diagnose relation between a medical test and a medical condition it is employed to identify. Also called diagnoses, identifies condition, screens for. Examples: "MedicalTest 'MRI' usedToDiagnose 'Brain Tumor'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Test' usedToDiagnose 'Anemia'", "MedicalTest 'X-ray' usedToDiagnose 'Fracture'".

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: vehicleSpecialUsage
candidates.comment: A vehicle special usage relation between a vehicle and an indication of whether it has been used for special purposes like commercial rental or as a taxi. Also called special use, commercial use, past usage. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Taxi'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Commercial Rental'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Driving School'".

candidates.label: permittedUsage
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the allowed uses or activities within an accommodation. Also called allowed uses, usage rules, permitted activities. Examples: An apartment has a permitted usage of 'Residential Only'. A hotel room has a permitted usage of 'Short-term Stay'. A conference hall has a permitted usage of 'Events and Meetings'.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: downvoteCount
candidates.comment: A downvote count relation between a comment and the integer representing the number of downvotes it has received. Also called "dislike count", "negative votes". Examples: "Comment 'This is wrong' downvoteCount '5'", "Answer downvoteCount '2'", "Review downvoteCount '10'".

candidates.label: flightDistance
candidates.comment: A flight distance relation between a flight and the total distance covered during its journey. Also called: journey distance, air travel distance, flight length. Examples: "Flight UA123" flight distance "1500 miles", "Flight BA456" flight distance "2400 km", "Flight LH789" flight distance "Long-haul".

candidates.label: loser
candidates.comment: A losing participant relation between a win action and the person who lost. Also called: defeated participant, vanquished, runner-up. Examples: "Chess Match WinAction loser Opponent B", "Race WinAction loser Second Place Runner", "Debate WinAction loser Team B".

candidates.label: duringMedia
candidates.comment: A during media relation between a how-to direction and a media object or URL representing the circumstances while performing this direction. Also called "instructional media", "step-by-step video", "visual guide". Examples: "How-to direction 'Attach part A' duringMedia 'Video of assembly'", "Direction 'Stir mixture' duringMedia 'Image of stirring technique'".

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: aircraft
candidates.comment: An aircraft relation between a flight and the specific type of vehicle used for air travel. Also called airplane type, plane model, flight vehicle. Examples: "A flight's aircraft is 'Boeing 747'.", "The flight uses an 'Airbus A320'."

candidates.label: knownVehicleDamages
candidates.comment: A vehicle condition relation between a vehicle and a textual description of its known damages, whether repaired or not. Also called vehicle damage report, damage history, known defects, condition notes. Examples: A used car has knownVehicleDamages 'minor dent on rear bumper'. A vehicle has knownVehicleDamages 'repaired fender bender'. A truck has knownVehicleDamages 'scratches on passenger side door'. Distinct from vehicleCondition, which is a general assessment, not specific damages.

candidates.label: cvdNumC19Died
candidates.comment: A mortality count relation between a CDCPMD record and the number of patients with suspected or confirmed COVID-19 who died in the hospital, ED, or overflow location. Also called: COVID-19 deaths, C19 fatalities, pandemic deaths. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num c19 died "10", "Facility B Report" cvd num c19 died "3", "Medical Center C" cvd num c19 died "25".

candidates.label: verificationFactCheckingPolicy
candidates.comment: A verification fact-checking policy relation between a news media organization or organization and a disclosure about its verification and fact-checking processes. Also called fact-checking policy, verification standards, editorial policy. Examples: "NewsMediaOrganization verificationFactCheckingPolicy 'https://example.com/fact-check-policy'", "Organization verificationFactCheckingPolicy 'Our journalists verify all claims.'", "News outlet verificationFactCheckingPolicy 'https://example.com/editorial-standards'".

candidates.label: confirmationNumber
candidates.comment: An identification relation for an invoice or order, providing a number that confirms its receipt. Also called "order confirmation", "booking reference", "receipt number". Examples: "Online order confirmationNumber 'ABC-12345'", "Flight invoice confirmationNumber 'XYZ-67890'".

candidates.label: recognizedBy
candidates.comment: A recognition relation between a credential and the organization that acknowledges its validity or value. Also called accredited by, validated by, acknowledged by. Examples: "A university degree is recognized by 'the Ministry of Education'.", "A professional certification is recognized by 'an industry association'.", "A medical license is recognized by 'the Medical Board'."

candidates.label: validIn
candidates.comment: A valid in relation between a certification, credential, or permit and the geographic area where it is valid. Also called valid region, applicable area, geographic validity. Examples: "Permit validIn 'California'", "Certification validIn 'European Union'", "Credential validIn 'United States'".

candidates.label: validFor
candidates.comment: A valid for relation between a credential or permit and the duration of its validity. Also called duration of validity, valid period, effective duration. Examples: "Permit validFor 'P1Y'", "Credential validFor 'P5Y'", "License validFor 'P6M'".

candidates.label: authenticator
candidates.comment: An organization responsible for authenticating a user's subscription to a media subscription. Also called: subscription authenticator, access provider, verification organization. Examples: "MediaSubscription 'Streaming Service' authenticator 'Cable Provider'", "MediaSubscription 'News App' authenticator 'Satellite Company'."

candidates.label: validFrom
candidates.comment: A valid from relation between a certification, demand, financial incentive, location feature specification, monetary amount, offer, opening hours specification, permit, or price specification and the date it becomes valid. Also called effective date, start date, activation date. Examples: "Offer validFrom '2023-11-01'", "Permit validFrom '2023-01-01T09:00:00'", "OpeningHoursSpecification validFrom '2024-01-01'". Distinct from validThrough or validUntil, which specify the end of validity.

candidates.label: validUntil
candidates.comment: A valid until relation between a permit and the date it ceases to be valid. Also called permit expiration date, permit end date, validity end date. Examples: "Permit validUntil '2024-06-30'", "Permit validUntil '2025-01-01'", "Permit validUntil '2023-12-31'". Distinct from validThrough, which is a more general property for various items.

candidates.label: validThrough
candidates.comment: A valid through relation between a demand, financial incentive, job posting, location feature specification, monetary amount, offer, or opening hours specification and the date after which it is no longer valid. Also called expiration date, end date, valid until. Examples: "Offer validThrough '2023-12-31'", "JobPosting validThrough '2023-11-30'", "OpeningHoursSpecification validThrough '2024-12-31'". Distinct from validFrom, which specifies the start of validity. Distinct from validUntil, which is similar but for Permit only.

candidates.label: dateSent

candidates.label: dateCreated

candidates.label: dateReceived
